question:
In a three-dimensional mathematical model, two long parallel wires are represented by the lines $$L_1:\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)$$ and $$L_2:\vec r=(3\hat i+\hat j+4\hat k)+\mu(2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k).$$ A point $T(3,1,4)$ lies on $L_2$. The class wants to calculate the separation of the wires and then confirm it geometrically by dropping a perpendicular from $T$ to $L_1$. If $P$ denotes the foot of this perpendicular on $L_1$, the segment $TP$ must be perpendicular to the common direction of the two lines.

(a) Verify that $L_1$ and $L_2$ are parallel.

(b) Calculate the shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$.

(c) Determine the coordinates of the foot $P$ of the perpendicular from $T$ to $L_1$.

(d) Verify that the length $TP$ is equal to the shortest distance obtained in part (b).
explanation:
(a)
The direction vector of both lines is
$$\vec b=(2,-1,2).$$
Since their direction vectors are identical, $L_1$ and $L_2$ are parallel.

(b)
Take points on the two lines with position vectors
$$\vec a_1=(1,2,3),\quad \vec a_2=(3,1,4).$$
For two parallel lines, the distance is
$$d=\frac{|\vec b\times(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)|}{|\vec b|}.$$
Now,
$$\vec a_2-\vec a_1=(2,-1,1).$$
Therefore,
$$\vec b\times(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)=(2,-1,2)\times(2,-1,1)=(1,2,0).$$
Hence,
$$|\vec b\times(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)|=\sqrt{5}$$
and
$$|\vec b|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+2^2}=3.$$
Thus, the shortest distance is
$$d=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\text{ units}.$$

(c)
A general point $P$ on $L_1$ is
$$P=(1+2\lambda,2-\lambda,3+2\lambda).$$
Since $TP$ is perpendicular to the direction vector $(2,-1,2)$, we require
$$\overrightarrow{PT}\cdot(2,-1,2)=0.$$
Now,
$$\overrightarrow{PT}=(2-2\lambda,-1+\lambda,1-2\lambda).$$
Therefore,
$$2(2-2\lambda)-(-1+\lambda)+2(1-2\lambda)=0.$$
Simplifying,
$$7-9\lambda=0,$$
so
$$\lambda=\frac{7}{9}.$$
Hence,
$$P=\left(1+\frac{14}{9},2-\frac{7}{9},3+\frac{14}{9}\right)=\left(\frac{23}{9},\frac{11}{9},\frac{41}{9}\right).$$

(d)
Using $T=(3,1,4)$ and $P=\left(\frac{23}{9},\frac{11}{9},\frac{41}{9}\right)$,
$$\overrightarrow{PT}=\left(\frac{4}{9},-\frac{2}{9},-\frac{5}{9}\right).$$
Therefore,
$$TP=\sqrt{\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)^2+\left(-\frac{2}{9}\right)^2+\left(-\frac{5}{9}\right)^2}.$$
Thus,
$$TP=\frac{\sqrt{45}}{9}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{9}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\text{ units}.$$
This equals the shortest distance found in part (b), verifying the result.

(b) Shortest distance $=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$
(c) $P=\left(\frac{23}{9},\frac{11}{9},\frac{41}{9}\right)$
(d) $TP=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$, confirming the result
